items.stem: Which best describes a sound approach to global HR policy?

options.text: Standardize where it adds value and localize where law or culture requires
options.rationale: Correct: effective global HR balances consistency with local adaptation.

options.text: Apply the headquarters country's rules everywhere without change
options.rationale: Ignoring local law and culture creates legal and engagement risk.

options.text: Let every site invent fully independent policies
options.rationale: No alignment loses the benefits of a global framework.

options.text: Avoid written policy to stay flexible
options.rationale: Lack of policy increases inconsistency and risk.

items.explanation: Correct: effective global HR balances consistency with local adaptation.
items.domain_ref: Global HR strategy and organizational effectiveness
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An employee is sent on a two-year assignment abroad. Which element is essential in the package?

options.text: Mobility, tax and compliance support, not only a converted salary
options.rationale: Correct: international assignments require mobility and compliance support.

options.text: Only a currency conversion of base pay
options.rationale: Salary conversion ignores assignment and compliance costs.

options.text: A promise to ignore the host country's employment law
options.rationale: Host-country law still applies and cannot be ignored.

options.text: No documentation to keep it flexible

items.explanation: Correct: international assignments require mobility and compliance support.

items.stem: Select TWO obligations that typically differ by country and must be checked locally.

options.rationale: Correct: statutory benefits vary widely by jurisdiction.
Correct: data-privacy rules differ significantly across countries.

Branding is unrelated to legal obligations.
Chart layout is not a statutory obligation.
